title: Stormglass Gambit
brief: A battle theme for a game, led by synthesizers on Surge XT: high energy, about three minutes, a seamless loop. The lead is a synthesizer. Heard on repeat: a hook that holds up, a section that contrasts, and a build back into the top.

sections.intent: The top of the loop: the hook on the lead synth over four-on-the-floor, rolling bass and tresillo arpeggio; a 16-bar period, each half a sentence ending on V.
A drop in register and density: a syncopated G-pedal riff in bass and riff synth with a flat second, broken kick; the lead answers from bar 25 with a repeated-note motif and climbs.
The hook returns fuller: a counter-line answers it, then the lead plays it a third higher over the counter synth playing the original; the melody reaches Eb6.
Development, leaner than hook_b (no pad, two stabs a bar): a one-bar idea in rising sequence over a stepwise rising bass, the counter synth echoing it, a broad answer and the Neapolitan.
The high point: the repeated-note motif in rising sequence to F6 (bar 60) in thirds, pad and riff synth added, ride and open hats, the Neapolitan for two bars, then a full stop on V.
The contrasting section: half-time, no four-on-the-floor, a slow sung theme on a square lead over pads in E-flat; its last eight bars state the hook at half speed.
The build back into the top, first stage: four-on-the-floor returns softly under an off-beat bass, the arpeggio plays only the hook's 3+3+2 accents, the lead hints the call.
Second stage: the repeated-note motif climbs two bars at a time through iv-VI-VII-bII; rolling bass, clap, the riff synth and the arpeggio open their filters.

Third stage: eight bars of dominant pedal with a cadential six-four, the call's head once then twice a bar, a snare roll doubling in rate, a rising swell; no kick or bass in the last bar, and the pickup D-E-F# into bar 1.

decisions: Style: electronic/trance as the primary entry (148 BPM inside its sourced 120-150, minor key, a lead motif, rapid arpeggios, a break and a build with a snare roll). The form axis is borrowed from game/battle because the brief asks for a game loop that goes round again with no ending, not a DJ track with a sparse intro and outro.
Tempo 148 BPM, 4/4, G minor, 112 bars = 181.6 s. The piece loops from bar 1: no intro, so one pass of the loop is the preview and the top of the loop is the hook itself.

The hook (bars 1-2): a 3+3+2 call G5-D5-Bb5 with an appoggiatura A5 falling to G5, and a stepwise tail. It is the only material of hook_a and hook_b; the riff section and the build use a second, repeated-note motif.

High point planned at bars 57-62 (the climax section): the melody's highest note F6 in bar 60, the fullest texture (pad and riff synth added, ride and open hats), then the Neapolitan A-flat and a stop on the dominant in bar 64. The contrast section is where it settles.

Contrast (bars 65-88): half time, relative-major side (Ebmaj7, Bb/D, Cm7, F), a square lead, no kick on every beat; reached by a deceptive move D to E-flat. Its last eight bars play the hook at half speed.

Seam: the last bar is D7 after a cadential six-four, so G, B-flat, D and A (the pitch classes of bar 1's first second) all sound in the last three bars. Kick and bass leave for the last bar only and return on bar 1; the snare roll, the riser, the arpeggio and the lead's pickup D-E-F# carry across. No tempo change.
Levels are written from the lead down; kick ducking on pad, bass, stabs, riff and arpeggio (release about an eighth note at 148 BPM). Delivered at -14 LUFS: the in-game level is set in the engine.
Player-like deviation is applied small (drums 0.8 ms, bass 1.2 ms, lead 3.5 ms): sequenced synthesizers.

Drums are written by hand on a step grid (not from musiclib.blocks): four-on-the-floor for the hook sections, a broken kick for the riff, half time for the contrast, a snare roll doubling in rate through the last eight bars.
authorship: Composed note by note by Claude with the music-production skill 0.6.0; no outside material.
revision_history: r1: first full render. Before it, two score reviews: chord symbols corrected to what sounds (Eb for the hook's bar 3, Gm7 for the riff's answer bar), the pad voiced against the arpeggio and the held melody notes and kept under the counter synth, contrast bass pickups made chord tones, breaths added to the lead, the chase thinned in its first half and filled in its second. Sounds chosen by audition figures.

r2: from r1's measurements. The build's last 400 ms measured 6.1 dB louder than the first 400 ms of the top: riser 7 dB down, snare roll and toms softer, arpeggio, pad and stabs held back in the last eight bars. The contrast theme measured 1.7 dB under its accompaniment and the section had 0.7% of its power above 2.5 kHz: the sine lead (0.5% above 2 kHz, unchanged by saturation) replaced by a square lead (28% above 2 kHz on the theme), bass and pad down there, hats up, a shaker added, the arpeggio's low-pass opened. The chase was not louder than hook_b: its second half is now a section of its own (climax) with ride, open hats, another crash, lead and counter up 1 dB and the riff synth's doubling down. More reverb on every send (the mix measured a clarity of +29 dB). Counter bar 36 rewritten on chord tones. Drums up 1 dB. Sections split for measuring and for cue points.

r3: from r2's measurements. The seam still fell 2.9 dB from the last 400 ms to the first: toms, snare roll, the last reverse crash and the riser softer again, the riff synth 2 dB down over the pedal, the top's crash and impact harder. The climax's lead measured 0.7 dB under its accompaniment: lead +1.8 dB there, stabs softer, riff doubling 1.5 dB further down. The lead's answers in the riff section (1.9 dB under) written as loud as the hook, riff synth 3 dB down under them. The first build stage measured 3.3 dB under the contrast before it: arpeggio filter opened further, lead hint and pad up. Bass 1 dB down, stabs and pad 1 dB up (250-800 Hz held 9% of the hook's power). Counter bar 36 moved to sixths under the lead (r2's rewrite doubled it at the octave).

r4 (the full render): r3's seam still fell 2.4 dB. Measured stem by stem over the last 400 ms, the two swells together stood as loud as the lead bus (-19.5 against -19.3 dBFS RMS) and the stabs 4 dB over their level in the first 400 ms: reverse crashes 3 dB down and the last one 4 dB more, the riser 4 dB down, the last two bars' stabs softer.
